chunks: Abu al-Abbas said: Hibatullah ibn Muhammad, son of the daughter of Umm Kulthum, daughter of Abu Ja'far al-Amari, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me from his teachers, who said:

The Shia always remained firm in the uprightness of Uthman ibn Sa'id (and Muhammad ibn Uthman, may Allah have mercy on them, until Abu Amr Uthman ibn Sa'id passed away), may Allah have mercy on him. His son, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman, performed his funeral bath and took charge of his affairs, with all matters referred to him. The Shia were unanimous in his uprightness, trustworthiness, and honesty, due to the prior explicit designation of his honesty and uprightness, and the command to refer to him during the lifetime of Hasan (peace be upon him) and after his death during the lifetime of his father, Uthman ibn Sa'id. There was no dispute regarding his uprightness, nor doubt about his honesty. The letters (tawqi'at) came out through him to the Shia in important matters throughout his life, in the same handwriting as they were during the lifetime of his father, Uthman. The Shia knew no one else in this matter and did not refer to anyone other than him.
ai.seo_question: Who were the primary emissaries of the Imam during the Minor Occultation and how was their authority verified?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the institutional continuity of the Shia community's reliance on the four Deputies, specifically highlighting Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri as the primary authority whose seal and handwriting authenticated the Imam's communications. It emphasizes that the community's consensus (*ijma'*) on his justice and trustworthiness was rooted in explicit textual evidence (*nass*) and practical governance during the Minor Occultation, ensuring no ambiguity in referring religious matters to him. This establishes the Deputies not merely as messengers but as the definitive, undisputed reference point for the Shia during the Imam's absence.
